newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas holds despite India award.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas holds despite India award.

text.p: Naphtha edged down on Monday in correction while gasoline held steady despite a lower Indian purchase, traders said.

State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) on Friday awarded its tender to buy its second cargo of 25,000-tonnes of 87-octane leaded gasoline for June at over $30 per tonne premium to MidEast naphtha quotes, a source close to IOC said.
The source said the premium was in the "low $30s" and lower than rumours on Friday of around $38.

The award, on a cost-and-freight (c+f) basis to Bombay on the west coast for delivery June 26-30, was also much lower than than IOC's first purchase in June at $43 per tonne over MidEast naphtha quotes, c+f Bombay June 18-22, the source said.

"But it still looks like a good number," said a trader with a major oil company who calculated the netback to $23.25 per barrel fob Singapore or 70 cents per barrel below Singapore 92-octane spot quotes.

The source said there were outstanding gasoline requirements from India as IOC's second June purchase arose from the five-day emergency shutdown on June 2 of the 150,000 barrels-per-day Cochin refinery.

Talk on fob Singapore barrels was thin as traders said they were now focusing on Taiwan's tender for 250,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded reformate for delivery July 24-August 15 which closes on Tuesday and is valid for two days.
Naphtha July swaps fell 10-15 cents per barrel to $21.10/$21.30.
"Prices went up too fast on Friday," a trader said. "It should come off in correction."
But market talk centred on Singapore floating premiums after a U.S. major on Friday sold a MR cargo for early July lifting at 60-70 cents per barrel over spot quotes, fob Singapore.
Some traders still claimed the level too high, assessing premiums morre around the 40-50 cents level.
But others said the premiums for July barrels were being hoisted up in preparation for August demand into north Asia, when petrochemical plants return from turnarounds.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
